subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should an explicit managed-service disable for OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM override persisted generated service-env values, or should persisted state-dir/config service env remain authoritative until edited?
rationale: Raw-stream logs may contain prompts, tool output, and user data, so automation should not choose the sensitive logging precedence contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Explicit Disable Wins
options.body: Treat unset, 0, false, and off as authoritative for managed-service disable, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

options.title: Persisted Env Wins
options.body: Keep state-dir .env and config env as the durable source and document that operators must edit those persisted values before restart disables raw-stream logging.

options.title: Doctor-Guided Repair Only
options.body: Leave runtime precedence mostly unchanged but add status/doctor checks that warn and repair stale raw-stream service-env values before operators believe logging is off.

recommendation.title: Explicit Disable Wins
recommendation.body: Treat unset, 0, false, and off as authoritative for managed-service disable, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest cross-path history across durable service env helpers and LaunchAgent lifecycle handling.
